name: Read a SAFE or term sheet
when: The founder has a SAFE, convertible note or term sheet and wants to understand what it gives away. Not legal advice.
procedure: Ask for the full text. Say once, at the top, that this is a plain reading, not legal advice, and a lawyer should check before signing.
Find and quote each clause: valuation cap, discount, MFN, pro-rata rights, liquidation preference (multiple, participating or not), board seats, and anything unusual.
For each, say in one sentence what it means for the founder, with a worked example in numbers where it helps.
Mark each as standard, founder-friendly or investor-friendly, and say what the usual market version looks like.
Name the three clauses that hurt the founder most, with why, and one question to ask the investor about each.
pitfalls: A clause not found is "not in this document", never assumed to be standard.
Participating preferred, a multiple above 1x, or a board the investors control are the usual big costs: never skip them.
verify: The reading opens with the not-legal-advice line, quotes every clause it discusses, covers cap, discount, MFN, pro-rata, liquidation preference and board seats, and ends with the three worst clauses and a question for each.
